ipc_description: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. Murder is defined as culpable homicide amounting to murder under the conditions specified in Section 300 of the IPC.
ipc_punishment: Death or imprisonment for life + fine
bns_description: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. The provision retains the same substantive punishment as the erstwhile IPC Section 302.

ipc_description: Culpable homicide is murder if the act by which the death is caused is done with the intention of causing death, or if it is done with the intention of causing such bodily injury as the offender knows to be likely to cause death, or if the bodily injury intended is sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death, or if the act is so imminently dangerous that it must in all probability cause death.
ipc_punishment: Defined under Section 302
bns_description: Culpable homicide is murder under the same four conditions as previously enumerated in IPC Section 300. The BNS consolidates the definition and punishment for murder within Section 101.

ipc_title: Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder
ipc_description: Whoever commits culpable homicide not amounting to murder shall, if the act is done with the intention of causing death or such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, be punished with imprisonment for life or imprisonment up to ten years and fine. If the act is done with the knowledge that it is likely to cause death but without any intention to cause death, punishment is imprisonment up to ten years, or fine, or both.
ipc_punishment: Part I: Imprisonment for life or up to 10 years + fine; Part II: Up to 10 years or fine or both
bns_title: Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder
bns_description: Whoever commits culpable homicide not amounting to murder shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine, if the act is done with intention. If done with knowledge only, imprisonment up to ten years, or fine, or both.

ipc_description: Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. This section covers cases of accidental death due to negligence.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both
bns_description: Whoever causes death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide shall be punished with imprisonment up to five years and fine. Sub-section (2) provides enhanced punishment of up to ten years if the person escapes without reporting to a police officer or Magistrate, introducing a new accountability provision.

ipc_description: Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called dowry death.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment not less than 7 years extendable to imprisonment for life
bns_description: Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband in connection with demand for dowry, such death shall be called dowry death. The husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death.

ipc_description: Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. If hurt is caused, the offender shall be liable to imprisonment for life or such punishment as is hereinbefore mentioned.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years + fine; if hurt caused: imprisonment for life
bns_description: Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. If hurt is caused to any person by such act, the offender shall be liable to either imprisonment for life, or imprisonment and fine.

ipc_description: Whoever attempts to commit suicide and does any act towards the commission of such offence, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both. Note: This section was effectively decriminalized by the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 (Section 115).
ipc_punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 1 year or fine or both (decriminalized by Mental Healthcare Act 2017)
bns_description: The BNS 2023 does not include a corresponding provision for attempt to commit suicide. The act has been fully decriminalized, aligning with the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, which presumes that a person attempting suicide is under severe stress and shall not be tried or punished under any law.

ipc_description: Whoever, except in the case provided for by Section 334, voluntarily causes hurt shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to ₹1000 or both
bns_description: Whoever, except in the case provided for by Section 122, voluntarily causes hurt shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both. The fine amount has been enhanced from the erstwhile IPC provision.

ipc_title: Punishment for voluntarily causing grievous hurt
ipc_description: Whoever, except in the case provided for by Section 335, voluntarily causes grievous hurt shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. Grievous hurt includes emasculation, permanent privation of sight or hearing, fractures, and other serious injuries.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years + fine
bns_title: Punishment for voluntarily causing grievous hurt
bns_description: Whoever, except in the case provided for by Section 124, voluntarily causes grievous hurt shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. The provision substantially retains the IPC framework for grievous hurt offences.

ipc_title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means
ipc_description: Whoever, except in the case provided for by Section 335, voluntarily causes grievous hurt by means of any instrument for shooting, stabbing or cutting, or any instrument which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death, or by means of fire, heated substance, poison, or any corrosive substance, or any explosive substance, or any substance deleterious to the human body, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment for life or up to 10 years + fine
bns_title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means
bns_description: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt by means of any instrument for shooting, stabbing or cutting, or any instrument which used as a weapon of offence is likely to cause death, or by means of fire or any heated substance, or by means of any poison or any corrosive substance, or any explosive or deleterious substance, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

ipc_title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid
ipc_description: Whoever causes permanent or partial damage or deformity to, or burns or maims or disfigures or disables any part or parts of the body of a person, or causes grievous hurt by throwing acid on or by administering acid to that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and with fine.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment not less than 10 years extendable to life + fine
bns_title: Causing grievous hurt by use of acid
bns_description: Whoever causes permanent or partial damage or deformity to, or burns or maims or disfigures or disables any part or parts of the body of a person or causes grievous hurt by throwing acid on or by administering acid to that person, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and with fine. The fine shall be just and reasonable to meet the medical expenses of the treatment of the victim.

ipc_description: Whoever makes any gesture, or any preparation intending or knowing it to be likely that such gesture or preparation will cause any person present to apprehend that he who makes that gesture or preparation is about to use criminal force to that person, is said to commit an assault. Words alone do not amount to an assault, but the words used may give to the gestures or preparation such meaning as may make them amount to an assault.
ipc_punishment: Defined — punishment under Section 352
bns_description: Whoever makes any gesture or any preparation intending or knowing it to be likely that such gesture or preparation will cause any person present to apprehend that he who makes that gesture or preparation is about to use criminal force to that person, is said to commit an assault. Mere words do not amount to an assault.

ipc_title: Punishment for assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation
ipc_description: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person otherwise than on grave and sudden provocation given by that person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to ₹500 or both
bns_title: Punishment for assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation
bns_description: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person otherwise than on grave and sudden provocation given by that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

ipc_description: Kidnapping is of two kinds: kidnapping from India and kidnapping from lawful guardianship. This section defines the two categories of kidnapping recognized under the Indian Penal Code.
ipc_punishment: Defined — punishment under Sections 363-369
bns_description: Kidnapping is of two kinds: kidnapping from India and kidnapping from lawful guardianship. The BNS retains the dual classification of kidnapping as established under the former IPC framework.

ipc_description: Whoever kidnaps any person from India or from lawful guardianship shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years + fine
bns_description: Whoever kidnaps any person from India or from lawful guardianship shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. The provision retains the same penalty structure as the erstwhile IPC.

ipc_title: Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty
ipc_description: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment not less than 1 year extendable to 5 years + fine
bns_title: Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty
bns_description: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.

ipc_title: Sexual harassment and punishment for sexual harassment
ipc_description: A man committing any of the following acts: physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures, a demand or request for sexual favours, showing pornography against the will of a woman, or making sexually coloured remarks, shall be guilty of the offence of sexual harassment.
ipc_punishment: Rigorous imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both (for acts 1-3); Imprisonment up to 1 year or fine or both (for act 4)
bns_title: Sexual harassment and punishment for sexual harassment
bns_description: A man committing any of the following acts: physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures; a demand or request for sexual favours; showing pornography against the will of a woman; or making sexually coloured remarks, shall be guilty of sexual harassment. Punishment varies based on the nature of the act committed.

ipc_description: Any man who watches, or captures the image of a woman engaging in a private act in circumstances where she would usually have the expectation of not being observed either by the perpetrator or by any other person at the behest of the perpetrator, or disseminates such image, shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of not less than one year extendable to three years and fine, and for second or subsequent conviction with imprisonment of not less than three years extendable to seven years and fine.
ipc_punishment: First conviction: 1-3 years + fine; Subsequent: 3-7 years + fine
bns_description: Any man who watches or captures the image of a woman engaging in a private act in circumstances where she would usually have the expectation of not being observed, or disseminates such image, shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment not less than one year extendable to three years and fine, and on subsequent conviction with imprisonment not less than three years extendable to seven years and fine.

ipc_description: Any man who follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by such woman, or monitors the use by a woman of the internet, email or any other form of electronic communication, commits the offence of stalking. Exceptions exist for acts done for prevention or detection of crime.
ipc_punishment: First conviction: up to 3 years + fine; Subsequent: up to 5 years + fine
bns_description: Any man who follows a woman and contacts or attempts to contact such woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by such woman, or monitors the use by a woman of the internet, email or any other form of electronic communication, commits the offence of stalking. Punishment on first conviction is imprisonment up to three years with fine, and on subsequent conviction up to five years with fine.

ipc_description: A man is said to commit rape if he penetrates his penis, or inserts any object or a part of the body into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a woman, or makes her do so with him or any other person, or applies his mouth to the vagina, anus, urethra of a woman, or makes her do so, under circumstances including against her will, without her consent, with consent obtained by fear or intoxication, or when she is unable to communicate consent, or when she is under 18 years of age.
ipc_punishment: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 10 years extendable to life + fine (Section 376)
bns_description: A man is said to commit rape under the same circumstances as previously defined, including penetration, insertion of objects, or oral acts against the will or without the consent of the woman, or where consent was obtained through coercion, fear, intoxication, or misrepresentation. The age of consent remains eighteen years. The BNS retains the comprehensive definition introduced by the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 2013.

ipc_description: Whoever commits rape shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. Enhanced punishments are prescribed for gang rape, rape by persons in positions of authority, and repeat offenders.
ipc_punishment: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 10 years extendable to life + fine
bns_description: Whoever commits rape shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. The BNS provides enhanced and graduated punishments for aggravated forms of rape, gang rape, and rape of minors under various age thresholds.

ipc_title: Punishment for rape on woman under twelve years of age
ipc_description: Whoever commits rape on a woman under twelve years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life, and with fine, or with death.
ipc_punishment: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 20 years or life or death + fine
bns_title: Punishment for rape on woman under twelve years of age
bns_description: Whoever commits rape on a woman under twelve years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life, and with fine or with death. The BNS consolidates aggravated rape provisions under Section 65 with graduated sub-sections.

ipc_title: Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty
ipc_description: Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. Cruelty includes conduct which is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health, or harassment with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for property or valuable security.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years + fine
bns_title: Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty
bns_description: Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. Cruelty means any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health, or harassment of the woman with a view to coercing her or her relatives to meet any unlawful demand for property or valuable security.

ipc_description: Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft. The moving of the property is essential to complete the offence of theft.
ipc_punishment: Defined — punishment under Section 379
bns_description: Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft. The definition retains all essential ingredients of the offence as previously established under the IPC.

ipc_description: Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both
bns_description: Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. The BNS consolidates the definition and punishment of theft within Section 303.

ipc_description: Whoever intentionally puts any person in fear of any injury to that person, or to any other, and thereby dishonestly induces the person so put in fear to deliver to any person any property or valuable security, or anything signed or sealed which may be converted into a valuable security, commits extortion.
ipc_punishment: Defined — punishment under Section 384
bns_description: Whoever intentionally puts any person in fear of any injury to that person or to any other, and thereby dishonestly induces the person so put in fear to deliver to any person any property or valuable security, or anything signed or sealed which may be converted into a valuable security, commits extortion.

ipc_description: Whoever commits extortion shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both
bns_description: Whoever commits extortion shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. The BNS consolidates the definition and punishment of extortion within Section 308.

ipc_description: In all robbery there is either theft or extortion. When theft is robbery: theft is robbery if, in order to the committing of the theft, or in committing the theft, or in carrying away or attempting to carry away property obtained by the theft, the offender voluntarily causes or attempts to cause death, hurt, or wrongful restraint, or fear of instant death, hurt, or wrongful restraint.
ipc_punishment: Defined — punishment under Section 392
bns_description: In all robbery there is either theft or extortion. Theft becomes robbery when the offender causes or attempts to cause death, hurt, wrongful restraint, or fear thereof in committing or carrying away property. Extortion becomes robbery when the offender is in the presence of the person put in fear and commits extortion by putting that person in fear of instant death, hurt or wrongful restraint.

ipc_description: Whoever commits robbery shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. If the robbery is committed on the highway between sunset and sunrise, the imprisonment may extend to fourteen years.
ipc_punishment: Rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years + fine; on highway at night: up to 14 years
bns_description: Whoever commits robbery shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. If the robbery is committed on the highway between sunset and sunrise, the imprisonment may be extended to fourteen years.

ipc_description: Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, or dishonestly uses or disposes of that property in violation of any direction of law prescribing the mode in which such trust is to be discharged, or of any legal contract made touching the discharge of such trust, commits criminal breach of trust.
ipc_punishment: Defined — punishment under Section 406
bns_description: Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property or with any dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, or dishonestly uses or disposes of that property in violation of any direction of law prescribing the mode in which such trust is to be discharged, commits criminal breach of trust.

ipc_title: Punishment for criminal breach of trust
ipc_description: Whoever commits criminal breach of trust shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both
bns_title: Punishment for criminal breach of trust
bns_description: Whoever commits criminal breach of trust shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. The BNS consolidates the definition and punishment provisions.

ipc_title: Criminal breach of trust by public servant, banker, merchant or agent
ipc_description: Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property in his capacity of a public servant or in the way of his business as a banker, merchant, factor, broker, attorney or agent, commits criminal breach of trust in respect of that property, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment for life or up to 10 years + fine
bns_title: Criminal breach of trust by public servant, banker, merchant or agent
bns_description: Whoever, being entrusted with property in his capacity of a public servant or in the way of his business as a banker, merchant, factor, broker, attorney or agent, commits criminal breach of trust in respect of that property, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

ipc_description: Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property, or intentionally induces the person so deceived to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit if he were not so deceived, and which act or omission causes or is likely to cause damage or harm to that person in body, mind, reputation or property, is said to cheat.
ipc_punishment: Defined — punishment under Section 417
bns_description: Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property, or intentionally induces the person so deceived to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit if he were not so deceived, and which act or omission causes or is likely to cause damage or harm to that person in body, mind, reputation or property, is said to cheat.

ipc_title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
ipc_description: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years + fine
bns_title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
bns_description: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything signed or sealed and capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

ipc_description: Whoever with intent to cause, or knowing that he is likely to cause, wrongful loss or damage to the public or to any person, causes the destruction of any property, or any such change in any property or in the situation thereof as destroys or diminishes its value or utility, or affects it injuriously, commits mischief.
ipc_punishment: Defined — punishment under Section 426
bns_description: Whoever with intent to cause, or knowing that he is likely to cause, wrongful loss or damage to the public or to any person, causes the destruction of any property, or any such change in any property or in the situation thereof as destroys or diminishes its value or utility, or affects it injuriously, commits mischief.

ipc_description: Whoever commits mischief shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine, or with both.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 months or fine or both
bns_description: Whoever commits mischief shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine, or with both. The BNS consolidates the definition and punishment of mischief within Section 324.

ipc_description: Whoever enters into or upon property in the possession of another with intent to commit an offence or to intimidate, insult or annoy any person in possession of such property, or having lawfully entered into or upon such property, unlawfully remains there with intent thereby to intimidate, insult or annoy any such person, or with intent to commit an offence, is said to commit criminal trespass.
ipc_punishment: Defined — punishment under Section 447
bns_description: Whoever enters into or upon property in the possession of another with intent to commit an offence or to intimidate, insult or annoy any person in possession of such property, or having lawfully entered unlawfully remains there with similar intent, is said to commit criminal trespass.

ipc_description: Whoever commits criminal trespass shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to ₹500 or both
bns_description: Whoever commits criminal trespass shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both. The fine amount has been enhanced under the BNS.

ipc_description: Whoever by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or otherwise, brings or attempts to bring into hatred or contempt, or excites or attempts to excite disaffection towards the Government established by law in India, shall be punished with imprisonment for life and fine, or with imprisonment up to three years and fine, or with fine alone.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment for life + fine, or imprisonment up to 3 years + fine, or fine
bns_title: Acts endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
bns_description: The BNS replaces the colonial-era sedition law with a more specifically defined offence. Whoever purposely or knowingly, by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or by electronic communication or by use of financial means, or otherwise, excites or attempts to excite, secession or armed rebellion or subversive activities, or encourages feelings of separatist activities or endangers sovereignty or unity and integrity of India, or indulges in or commits any such act, shall be punished with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

ipc_description: When two or more persons agree to do, or cause to be done, an illegal act, or an act which is not illegal by illegal means, such an agreement is designated a criminal conspiracy. No agreement except an agreement to commit an offence shall amount to a criminal conspiracy unless some act besides the agreement is done by one or more parties to such agreement in pursuance thereof.
ipc_punishment: Defined — punishment under Section 120B
bns_description: When two or more persons agree to do, or cause to be done, an illegal act, or an act which is not illegal by illegal means, such an agreement is designated a criminal conspiracy. No agreement except an agreement to commit an offence shall amount to a criminal conspiracy unless some act besides the agreement is done by one or more parties in pursuance thereof. The BNS consolidates the definition and punishment within Section 61.

ipc_description: Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term of two years or upwards, shall be punished in the same manner as if he had abetted such offence. Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy other than a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable as aforesaid shall be punished with imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months, or with fine, or with both.
ipc_punishment: Same as abetment of the offence conspired; or up to 6 months + fine for lesser offences
bns_description: Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term of two years or upwards, shall be punished in the same manner as if he had abetted such offence. For conspiracies involving lesser offences, punishment is imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both.

ipc_description: Whenever force or violence is used by an unlawful assembly, or by any member thereof, in prosecution of the common object of such assembly, every member of such assembly is guilty of the offence of rioting.
ipc_punishment: Defined — punishment under Section 147
bns_description: Whenever force or violence is used by an unlawful assembly, or by any member thereof, in prosecution of the common object of such assembly, every member of such assembly is guilty of the offence of rioting. The BNS retains the essential elements of the offence of rioting.

ipc_description: Whoever is guilty of rioting shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both
bns_description: Whoever is guilty of rioting shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. The provision retains the same punishment as the erstwhile IPC.

ipc_description: Whoever is guilty of rioting, being armed with a deadly weapon or with anything which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both
bns_description: Whoever is guilty of rioting, being armed with a deadly weapon or with anything which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

ipc_description: Whoever offers, gives or agrees to give a gratification to any person as a motive or reward for such person or any other person to exercise any electoral right, or for inducing or attempting to induce any elector to vote or refrain from voting at an election, or any public servant to exercise or refrain from exercising any official function, commits bribery.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year or fine or both
bns_description: Whoever offers, gives or agrees to give a gratification to any person as a motive or reward for exercising any electoral right or for inducing or attempting to induce any elector to vote or refrain from voting at an election, commits the offence of bribery. The BNS retains electoral bribery provisions while anti-corruption offences by public servants are primarily governed by the Prevention of Corruption Act.

ipc_description: Whoever commits the offence of bribery shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both. A person who is bribed shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine or with both.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year or fine or both
bns_description: Whoever commits the offence of bribery shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both. Both the person offering and the person accepting the bribe are punishable.

ipc_description: Whoever, by words either spoken or intended to be read, or by signs or by visible representations, makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm, or knowing or having reason to believe that such imputation will harm, the reputation of such person, is said to defame that person. Ten exceptions are provided including imputations of truth for public good, conduct of public servants, and fair comments on public questions.
ipc_punishment: Defined — punishment under Section 500
bns_description: Whoever, by words either spoken or intended to be read, or by signs or by visible representations, makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm, or knowing or having reason to believe that such imputation will harm, the reputation of such person, is said to defame that person. The BNS retains the ten exceptions including truth published for public good and fair comment.

ipc_description: Whoever defames another shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. Defamation remains a criminal offence under Indian law in addition to being a civil wrong.
ipc_punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both
bns_description: Whoever defames another shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. The BNS retains criminal defamation with the same punishment framework, alongside community service as an alternative punishment option.

ipc_description: Whoever makes any false documents or false electronic record or part of a document or electronic record, with intent to cause damage or injury to the public or to any person, or to support any claim or title, or to cause any person to part with property, or to enter into any express or implied contract, or with intent to commit fraud or that fraud may be committed, commits forgery.
ipc_punishment: Defined — punishment under Section 465
bns_description: Whoever makes any false documents or false electronic record or part of a document or electronic record, with intent to cause damage or injury to the public or to any person, or to support any claim or title, or to cause any person to part with property, or with intent to commit fraud, commits forgery. The BNS explicitly includes electronic records in the definition.

ipc_description: Whoever commits forgery shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both
bns_description: Whoever commits forgery shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. The BNS consolidates the definition and punishment within Section 336.

ipc_description: Whoever commits forgery, intending that the document or electronic record forged shall be used for the purpose of cheating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years + fine
bns_description: Whoever commits forgery, intending that the document or electronic record forged shall be used for the purpose of cheating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. This provision addresses the aggravated form of forgery linked with cheating.

ipc_title: Counterfeiting currency notes or bank notes
ipc_description: Whoever counterfeits, or knowingly performs any part of the process of counterfeiting, any currency note or bank note, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment for life or up to 10 years + fine
bns_title: Counterfeiting currency notes or bank notes
bns_description: Whoever counterfeits, or knowingly performs any part of the process of counterfeiting, any currency note or bank note, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. The BNS retains stringent penalties for counterfeiting currency.

ipc_title: Using as genuine forged or counterfeit currency notes or bank notes
ipc_description: Whoever sells to, or buys or receives from, any other person, or otherwise traffics in or uses as genuine, any forged or counterfeit currency note or bank note, knowing or having reason to believe the same to be forged or counterfeit, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment for life or up to 10 years + fine
bns_title: Using as genuine forged or counterfeit currency notes or bank notes
bns_description: Whoever sells to, or buys or receives from, any other person, or otherwise traffics in or uses as genuine, any forged or counterfeit currency note or bank note, knowing or having reason to believe the same to be forged or counterfeit, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment up to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

ipc_title: Possession of forged or counterfeit currency notes or bank notes
ipc_description: Whoever has in his possession any forged or counterfeit currency note or bank note, knowing or having reason to believe the same to be forged or counterfeit and intending to use the same as genuine, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years or fine or both
bns_title: Possession of forged or counterfeit currency notes or bank notes
bns_description: Whoever has in his possession any forged or counterfeit currency note or bank note, knowing or having reason to believe the same to be forged or counterfeit and intending to use the same as genuine or that it may be used as genuine, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

ipc_title: Making or possessing instruments or materials for forging or counterfeiting currency notes or bank notes
ipc_description: Whoever makes, or performs any part of the process of making, or buys or sells or disposes of, or has in his possession, any machinery, instrument or material for the purpose of being used, or knowing or having reason to believe that it is intended to be used, for forging or counterfeiting any currency note or bank note, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment for life or up to 10 years + fine
bns_title: Making or possessing instruments or materials for counterfeiting
bns_description: Whoever makes, or performs any part of the process of making, or buys, sells, disposes of, or has in possession any machinery, instrument or material for the purpose of being used for forging or counterfeiting any currency note or bank note, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment up to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

ipc_description: Whoever sells, lets to hire, distributes, publicly exhibits or in any manner puts into circulation, or for purposes of sale, hire, distribution, public exhibition or circulation, makes, produces or has in his possession any obscene book, pamphlet, paper, drawing, painting, representation or figure or any other obscene object whatsoever, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to two years and with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees on first conviction, and on subsequent conviction with imprisonment up to five years and fine up to five thousand rupees.
ipc_punishment: First conviction: up to 2 years + fine up to ₹2000; Subsequent: up to 5 years + fine up to ₹5000
bns_description: Whoever sells, distributes, publicly exhibits or puts into circulation any obscene book, pamphlet, paper, drawing, painting, representation, figure or any other obscene object, or makes, produces or has in possession such material for purposes of sale, distribution, public exhibition or circulation, shall be punished. The BNS updates the provision to include electronic and digital forms of obscene material.

ipc_description: Whoever, to the annoyance of others, does any obscene act in any public place, or sings, recites or utters any obscene song, ballad or words, in or near any public place, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine, or with both.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 months or fine or both
bns_description: Whoever, to the annoyance of others, does any obscene act in any public place, or sings, recites or utters any obscene song, ballad or words, in or near any public place, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine, or with both.

ipc_description: A person is guilty of a public nuisance who does any act or is guilty of an illegal omission which causes any common injury, danger or annoyance to the public or to the people in general who dwell or occupy property in the vicinity, or which must necessarily cause injury, obstruction, danger or annoyance to persons who may have occasion to use any public right.
ipc_punishment: Defined — punishment under Sections 269-290
bns_description: A person is guilty of a public nuisance who does any act or is guilty of an illegal omission which causes any common injury, danger or annoyance to the public or to the people in general who dwell or occupy property in the vicinity. The BNS retains the broad definition of public nuisance with corresponding penalties.

ipc_title: Rash driving or riding on a public way
ipc_description: Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to ₹1000 or both
bns_title: Rash driving or riding on a public way
bns_description: Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both. The BNS retains this provision for public safety.

ipc_description: Whoever, fraudulently or dishonestly makes use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to rupees one lakh. This offence is covered under the Information Technology Act, 2000 and is cross-referenced for cybercrime mapping.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years + fine up to ₹1 lakh (IT Act Section 66C)
bns_description: Identity theft remains governed by Section 66C of the Information Technology Act, 2000. The BNS does not separately codify identity theft but the IT Act provision continues to operate for electronic identity fraud. Whoever fraudulently uses the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of another person is punishable under this provision.

ipc_title: Cheating by personation using computer resource (IT Act cross-reference)
ipc_description: Whoever, by means of any communication device or computer resource cheats by personation, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees. This section of the IT Act addresses cyber fraud through impersonation using electronic means.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years + fine up to ₹1 lakh (IT Act Section 66D)
bns_title: Cheating by personation using computer resource
bns_description: Cheating by personation using computer resources continues to be governed by Section 66D of the Information Technology Act, 2000. The BNS Section 318 (cheating) may also apply in conjunction with IT Act provisions when cyber fraud involves personation through electronic means. The IT Act provisions provide the specific framework for technology-facilitated fraud.

ipc_description: Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, or to the person or reputation of any one in whom that person is interested, with intent to cause alarm to that person, or to cause that person to do any act which he is not legally bound to do, or to omit to do any act which that person is legally entitled to do, as the means of avoiding the execution of such threat, commits criminal intimidation.
ipc_punishment: Defined — punishment under Section 506
bns_description: Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, or to the person or reputation of any one in whom that person is interested, with intent to cause alarm to that person, or to cause that person to do any act which he is not legally bound to do, or to omit to do any act which that person is legally entitled to do, commits criminal intimidation.

ipc_description: Whoever commits the offence of criminal intimidation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. If the threat is to cause death or grievous hurt, or to cause the destruction of any property by fire, or to cause an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, the offender shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
ipc_punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both; if threat of death/grievous hurt: up to 7 years
bns_description: Whoever commits criminal intimidation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. If the threat is to cause death or grievous hurt, or destruction of property by fire, or an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life or up to seven years, the punishment is imprisonment up to seven years, or fine, or both.

ipc_title: Acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention
ipc_description: When a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of the common intention of all, each of such persons is liable for that act in the same manner as if it were done by him alone. This section establishes the principle of constructive liability based on shared intention.
ipc_punishment: As per the offence committed with common intention
bns_title: Acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention
bns_description: When a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of the common intention of all, each of such persons is liable for that act in the same manner as if it were done by him alone. The BNS incorporates this foundational principle of joint criminal liability within Section 3, which deals with general explanations.

ipc_description: Whoever causes death by doing an act with the intention of causing death, or with the intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with the knowledge that he is likely by such act to cause death, commits the offence of culpable homicide. This section defines culpable homicide, distinguishing it from murder.
ipc_punishment: Defined — punishment under Section 304
bns_description: Whoever causes death by doing an act with the intention of causing death, or with the intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with the knowledge that he is likely by such act to cause death, commits the offence of culpable homicide. The BNS retains the tripartite definition of culpable homicide.
